reference_use.conclusion:
Pinned snapshot (project d09bc8a, Mathlib 25730c7c) plus the pinned simongmt package.

Found and used:
- Child A: MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero (μHE[0] = μH[0]), Measure.hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton, MeasureTheory.sum_measure_singleton, Set.encard_coe_eq_coe_finsetCard, Set.encard_eq_top_iff, ENat.toENNReal_top, ENNReal.eq_top_of_forall_nnreal_le, Set.Infinite.exists_subset_card_eq.
- Child B: Submodule.orthogonalProjectionOnto with starProjection_apply (definitional P = ↑ ∘ π), Submodule.lipschitzWith_orthogonalProjectionOnto, stdOrthonormalBasis with OrthonormalBasis.reindex (finCongr) and .repr, LinearIsometryEquiv.lipschitzWith, isometry_subtype_coe, Set.image_image, Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume.
- Parent assembly: ae_lt_top, ae_iff, measure_mono_null.

No match:
- Mathlib has no identity H⁰ = counting measure / encard (only singleton = 1 and 1 ≤ μH[0] s for nonempty s) and no isometric chart for starProjection.
- SimonGMT has neither. AppendixA has only dimH lemmas, Ch01 has simonHausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton, and Ch04 uses starProjection only for varifolds.
- dag.json has no name collision and no overlapping statement. The sibling cone_density_infinite children (bf_plane_closedBall_measure_eq, bf_plane_vitali_disjoint_cover) are different statements.

- Full child proofs and the parent assembly against the exact frozen parent type compile.

rationale:
Decision: split into two children. They do not depend on each other (depends_on = [] for both), and each is atomic.

Why. The printed proof of the selected node is M. G. Dall'Alba, The Besicovitch–Federer Projection Theorem (MSc thesis, Padova, 2020; https://www.math.unipd.it/~monti/tesi/DallAlba.pdf), Lemma 5.4, p. 70. It reads: "Recall that |A ∩ (V+a)| = H⁰(A ∩ (V+a)). This Lemma follows from Theorem 3.15: ∫*_{V⊥} H⁰(A ∩ Q_V⁻¹{y}) dHᵐ y ≤ c Hᵐ(A) < +∞, and we have that H⁰(A ∩ (V+y)) < +∞ for Hᵐ-almost all y ∈ V⊥." The thesis states Theorem 3.15 (Eilenberg) for Lipschitz maps into ℝᵐ with Lebesgue measure Lᵐ, just like the frozen hypothesis (Eil). Lemma 5.4, however, integrates with Hᵐ over the plane V⊥. The proof therefore has three ingredients, and the supplied parent proof follows them:
(A) H⁰ is counting measure. This is the "Recall" sentence and parent Step 4. It becomes child hausdorff_zero_counting, Submission.bf_hausdorffZero_eq_encard: ∀ N (S : Set (Rn N)), μHE[0] S = S.encard.
(B) The plane is identified isometrically with ℝⁿ, carrying Hⁿ to Lⁿ. The printed proof uses this tacitly; it is parent Steps 1 and 6. It becomes child projection_isometric_chart, Submission.bf_starProjection_isometricChart: there is a 1-Lipschitz f : ℝ^{n+ℓ} → ℝⁿ with f a = f b ⟺ P a = P b and Hⁿ(P(S)) = Lⁿ(f(S)) for every S.
(C) The measure-theoretic core, parent Steps 2, 3 and 5. It stays in the parent as a short assembly.

Both children are genuine, reusable textbook facts that the pinned libraries lack:
- Mathlib has only μH[0]{x} = 1, 1 ≤ μH[0] s for nonempty s, and μHE[0] = μH[0].
- SimonGMT has no counting-measure identity and no chart lemma for starProjection.
- (A) links H⁰-slices (Eilenberg, co-area) to the encard used in the contract's AreaFormula.
- (B) is the standard transfer between Hⁿ on an n-plane of ℝ^{n+ℓ} and Lⁿ on ℝⁿ.
- Neither child mentions infinite fibres or Eilenberg's inequality, so neither restates the parent or any other DAG node. A scan of dag.json (85 nodes) found no overlapping statement and no name collision.

Size trade-off: the complete Lean proof is about 80 lines (children about 22 and 33, assembly about 20). That is borderline, and several nodes of similar size in this run were ruled atomic. The split follows the sibling precedent cone_density_infinite, which split off a roughly 25-line plane-measure lemma for the same reasons. It isolates exactly the two library-gap facts from the core argument.

How the children give the selected statement by the supplied proof. Fix n, ℓ, W with finrank W = n, and A with Hⁿ(A) < ∞.
1. Take f from (B).
2. Apply (Eil) with (N, m, k) := (n+ℓ, n, 0), the set A, the map f and L := 1. This gives a measurable g with μHE[0](A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) ≤ g y for all y and ∫⁻ g ≤ (C·1ⁿ)·μHE[n+0](A) < ∞.
3. By ae_lt_top, g < ∞ Lⁿ-a.e., so Lⁿ{g = ∞} = 0.
4. For a ∈ A₃, (B)(ii) gives A ∩ f⁻¹{f a} = {b ∈ A : P b = P a}, which is infinite. By (A), μHE[0] of this set is its encard, which is ∞, so ∞ ≤ g(f a).
5. Hence f(A₃) ⊆ {g = ∞}, so Lⁿ(f(A₃)) = 0.
6. By (B)(iii), Hⁿ(P(A₃)) = Lⁿ(f(A₃)) = 0.

Machine check. Toolchain: pinned Lean 4.35.0-rc3 and Mathlib 25730c7c, running `lake env lean` on /tmp scratch files after `import GMT.Ch03.Submission`, in the contract's namespace and opens.
1. Both single-line child types elaborate.
2. The parent theorem, typed with the exact frozen lean_statement read programmatically from the handoff JSON, is proved in about 20 lines from Submission.bf_hausdorffZero_eq_encard and Submission.bf_starProjection_isometricChart alone.
3. Both children were fully proved with no sorry. `#print axioms` for all three declarations gives only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].

An independent reviewer then:
- re-ran the full file and got the same axioms;
- re-checked the assembly with the two child types declared as axioms;
- ran the verifier's contract_scope and validate_lean_statement on both child types;
- confirmed byte-identity of all types.
It accepted with no blocking findings. Its non-blocking suggestions were applied: child B was retitled, and this size trade-off is stated explicitly.

subproblems.title: Zero-dimensional Hausdorff measure is counting measure: H⁰(S) = #S on ℝ^N
subproblems.statement: For every N ∈ ℕ and every set S ⊆ ℝ^N = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) (arbitrary, not necessarily measurable), H⁰(S) = #S. Here H⁰ := μHE[0] is the zero-dimensional Euclidean Hausdorff (outer) measure, and #S := S.encard ∈ ℕ ∪ {∞} is the cardinality of S (∞ exactly when S is infinite), viewed in [0, ∞] via the coercion ℕ∞ → ℝ≥0∞. In particular, H⁰(S) = ∞ for every infinite S.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (S : Set (Rn N)), μHE[0] S = (S.encard : ℝ≥0∞)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. This is the first sentence of the printed proof of M. G. Dall'Alba, The Besicovitch–Federer Projection Theorem (Master's thesis, Università di Padova, 2020), Lemma 5.4, p. 70: “Recall that |A ∩ (V + a)| = H⁰(A ∩ (V + a))”, i.e. H⁰ is counting measure. The argument below is Step 4 of the parent proof, with the finite case made explicit so that the identity holds for every set.

Notation. Fix N ∈ ℕ and an arbitrary set S ⊆ ℝ^N = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N).
- μH[0] is Mathlib's unnormalized 0-dimensional Hausdorff measure on ℝ^N. Like every Mathlib measure, it applies to arbitrary sets as an outer measure and is monotone: T ⊆ T′ ⇒ μH[0](T) ≤ μH[0](T′).
- #S := S.encard ∈ ℕ ∪ {⊤}, mapped into [0, ∞] by the coercion ℕ∞ → ℝ≥0∞ (n ↦ n, ⊤ ↦ ∞).

1. Reduction to μH[0]. By Mathlib MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero, μHE[0] = μH[0] as measures on ℝ^N (the normalizing constant in dimension 0 equals 1). So it suffices to prove μH[0](S) = #S.

2. Singletons. For every x ∈ ℝ^N, μH[0]({x}) = 1 (Mathlib MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton).

3. Finite sets. Let t be a finite set of points of ℝ^N (a Finset).
- Every singleton {x} is closed, hence Borel measurable (ℝ^N has MeasurableSingletonClass).
- Singletons of distinct points are disjoint.
- So t is the finite disjoint union of the measurable sets {x}, x ∈ t.
Finite additivity of the measure μH[0] and step 2 give μH[0](t) = Σ_{x ∈ t} μH[0]({x}) = Σ_{x ∈ t} 1 = #t (Mathlib MeasureTheory.sum_measure_singleton: Σ_{x ∈ t} μ{x} = μ(t)).

4. Case S finite. Then S equals the finite set t := S.toFinset, and S.encard is the natural number #t (Mathlib Set.encard_coe_eq_coe_finsetCard), whose image in [0, ∞] is #t. By step 3, μH[0](S) = #t = #S.

5. Case S infinite.
- S.encard = ⊤ (Mathlib Set.encard_eq_top_iff), whose image in [0, ∞] is ∞ (ENat.toENNReal_top). So we must show μH[0](S) = ∞.
- By Mathlib ENNReal.eq_top_of_forall_nnreal_le, it suffices to show r ≤ μH[0](S) for every real r ≥ 0.
- Given r, put k := ⌈r⌉ ∈ ℕ, so r ≤ k (Nat.le_ceil).
- Since S is infinite, it contains a finite subset t with exactly k elements (Mathlib Set.Infinite.exists_subset_card_eq).
- By step 3 and monotonicity, r ≤ k = #t = μH[0](t) ≤ μH[0](S).
Hence μH[0](S) = ∞ = #S.

6. Conclusion. Steps 4 and 5 cover every S, so μH[0](S) = #S. By step 1, μHE[0](S) = (S.encard : [0, ∞]) for every N and every S ⊆ ℝ^N. ∎
proof_key_steps: Finite additivity over the measurable singletons gives μH[0](t) = #t for every finite t (sum_measure_singleton).
S finite: S = S.toFinset, so μH[0](S) = #S = S.encard.
S infinite: S.encard = ⊤. For each r ≥ 0, pick t ⊆ S with ⌈r⌉ elements; then r ≤ #t = μH[0](t) ≤ μH[0](S). Hence μH[0](S) = ∞.

subproblems.title: Isometric chart of the orthogonal projection onto an n-plane: a 1-Lipschitz f : ℝ^{n+ℓ} → ℝⁿ with the fibres of P and Hⁿ(P(S)) = Lⁿ(f(S))
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (W : Submodule ℝ (Rn (n + ℓ))), finrank ℝ W = n → ∃ f : Rn (n + ℓ) → Rn n, LipschitzWith 1 f ∧ (∀ a b : Rn (n + ℓ), f a = f b ↔ W.starProjection a = W.starProjection b) ∧ ∀ S : Set (Rn (n + ℓ)), μHE[n] (W.starProjection '' S) = volume (f '' S)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. This is Steps 1 and 6 of the parent proof. The printed proof of M. G. Dall'Alba, The Besicovitch–Federer Projection Theorem (Master's thesis, Università di Padova, 2020), Lemma 5.4, p. 70, applies Eilenberg's inequality (Theorem 3.15 there, stated for Lipschitz maps into ℝᵐ with Lebesgue measure Lᵐ) to the orthogonal projection onto the m-plane V^⊥ while integrating with Hᵐ over V^⊥. This tacitly identifies the plane isometrically with Euclidean space, and Hᵐ with Lᵐ. This lemma makes that identification explicit, with the n-plane W in place of V^⊥. (The parent proof writes its chart as ι : ℝⁿ ≃ W with f = ι⁻¹ ∘ π. Below, ι denotes the inverse direction W ≃ ℝⁿ, so f = ι ∘ π is the same map.)

Notation. N := n + ℓ.
- π : ℝ^N → W is the orthogonal projection viewed as a map into the subspace W (Mathlib W.orthogonalProjectionOnto).
- ↑ : W → ℝ^N is the inclusion.
- Then P x = ↑(π x) for all x, by definition (starProjection = subtypeL ∘ orthogonalProjectionOnto; Mathlib Submodule.starProjection_apply).
- W is finite-dimensional, hence complete, so the orthogonal projection exists.

1. A linear isometry ι : W ≃ ℝⁿ. W, with the inner product of ℝ^N, is a real inner product space of dimension n. Take an orthonormal basis of W indexed by Fin n: for instance Mathlib's stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ W, which is indexed by Fin (finrank ℝ W), reindexed along the bijection finCongr : Fin (finrank ℝ W) ≃ Fin n given by the hypothesis finrank ℝ W = n. Let ι : W → ℝⁿ be its coordinate map (OrthonormalBasis.repr), a linear isometric equivalence. Define
 f := ι ∘ π : ℝ^N → ℝⁿ and J := ↑ ∘ ι⁻¹ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^N.

2. (i) f is 1-Lipschitz.
- The orthogonal projection has operator norm ≤ 1, so π is 1-Lipschitz: |π x − π x′| = |π(x − x′)| ≤ |x − x′| (Mathlib Submodule.lipschitzWith_orthogonalProjectionOnto).
- ι is an isometry, hence 1-Lipschitz (LinearIsometryEquiv.lipschitzWith).
- Therefore f = ι ∘ π is (1·1 = 1)-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.comp).

3. (ii) The fibres of f are the fibres of P.
- If f a = f b, then π a = π b because ι is injective, hence P a = ↑(π a) = ↑(π b) = P b.
- Conversely, if P a = P b, i.e. ↑(π a) = ↑(π b), then π a = π b because the inclusion is injective (Subtype.ext), hence f a = ι(π a) = ι(π b) = f b.

4. Factorization P = J ∘ f. For every x ∈ ℝ^N, J(f x) = ↑(ι⁻¹(ι(π x))) = ↑(π x) = P x. Consequently, for every S ⊆ ℝ^N, P(S) = J(f(S)), since the image under a composite is the iterated image (Set.image_image).

5. J is an isometry. ι⁻¹ : ℝⁿ → W is an isometry, and the inclusion of the subspace W (with the induced metric) into ℝ^N is an isometry (isometry_subtype_coe). A composite of isometries is an isometry.

6. (iii) Measure transfer.
- Euclidean Hausdorff measures are invariant under isometries, applied to arbitrary sets: Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image gives μHE[d](J(T)) = μHE[d](T).
- Take d := n and T := f(S) ⊆ ℝⁿ. By step 4, Hⁿ(P(S)) = μHE[n](J(f(S))) = μHE[n](f(S)), the latter computed in ℝⁿ.
- On ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), μHE[n] = volume (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume n).
Hence Hⁿ(P(S)) = Lⁿ(f(S)) for every S ⊆ ℝ^N.

7. Conclusion. The map f of step 1 satisfies (i) by step 2, (ii) by step 3, and (iii) by step 6. ∎
proof_key_steps: An orthonormal basis of W indexed by Fin n gives a linear isometric equivalence ι : W ≃ ℝⁿ. Put f := ι ∘ π with π := W.orthogonalProjectionOnto, so that P = ↑ ∘ π.
f is 1-Lipschitz, because π has operator norm ≤ 1 and ι is an isometry.
f a = f b ⟺ π a = π b ⟺ P a = P b, by injectivity of ι and of the inclusion.
P = J ∘ f with J := ↑ ∘ ι⁻¹ an isometry, so P(S) = J(f(S)).
Isometry invariance of μHE[n] and μHE[n] = volume on ℝⁿ give Hⁿ(P(S)) = Lⁿ(f(S)).
